glossary.definition: The service’s defined commitment to handle work. In HarborDispatch, acceptance means a matching gateway row has committed; it does not mean the worker has completed.

A message reporting a particular stage of handling. Its meaning depends on the protocol: receipt, broker persistence, consumer handling, and business-effect commitment are different acknowledgement boundaries.
A decision about whether new work becomes the system’s responsibility, based on policy and available resources. Rejection should remain distinct from failure after durable acceptance.
The position through which committed changes have been incorporated into a replica’s serving state. Receiving or persisting a log entry does not necessarily mean queries already reflect it.
A stable reference to a specific built output, commonly associated with a checksum and provenance. A branch name alone can change and is not a complete artifact identity.
A result delivered after the initiating call has returned or suspended. Correct handling requires ownership of operation state and a rule for cancellation, stale generations, and cleanup.
The property that a defined group of state changes is committed together or not committed under the resource’s transaction model. It does not automatically include unrelated external effects.

The component or protocol entitled to decide a particular state transition. Architecture should identify authority for uniqueness, receipts, membership, credentials, and migration rather than assuming it from network location.
A delay policy between attempts, often increasing after repeated failure. Backoff reduces some retry pressure but does not by itself bound fleet-wide concurrency or make unsafe retries idempotent.
A mechanism that limits upstream production according to downstream capacity. It needs an explicit propagation and overload policy rather than merely moving work into another unbounded queue.

Compatibility among compiled components at their ABI boundary. Source compatibility, Pimpl, and matching function names do not automatically guarantee compatible object layout, runtimes, or allocation ownership.
A resource partition that limits how one work class can exhaust capacity needed by another. Its protection depends on shared resources below the partition as well as visible thread pools.
In the teaching model, the minimum acceptable version retained after invalidation. It prevents a late older fill from repopulating the cache after the old value was removed.
A representation of the fields that determine an operation’s meaning after validation and normalization. Duplicate recognition compares canonical meaning rather than incidental textual formatting.
A recorded recovery position or state. Its semantics must specify which work is complete; advancing past unfinished work can lose processing even when later work has finished.
A stateful admission policy for a dependency, often using closed, open, and half-open states. It limits repeated failing calls but does not repair the dependency or undo remote effects.
The point at which a resource reports that a transaction or state transition is committed under its guarantees. Client observation of that commit is a separate event.
A new business action intended to address a previous partial effect. It may not restore the exact prior world and requires its own identity, failure handling, and verification.
Agreement on decisions under a defined distributed failure model. Broadcasting messages or assigning a leader number does not implement the complete protocol and its safety and progress conditions.
The contract governing which observations and orderings clients may see. It should be expressed through operation histories, not only vague terms such as strong or current.
A position in a particular log partition or stream. It is a transport coordinate and should not automatically replace a domain event identifier that must survive export or replay.
Metadata connecting observations related to work. A job key, attempt ID, and trace ID can be correlated while retaining different scopes and lifetimes.
The latest eligible completion or waiting boundary under a defined clock and policy. A caller’s expired wait does not prove that a remote mutation did not commit.
A controlled path for work that cannot complete under ordinary retry policy. It needs ownership, retention, diagnosis, and authorized redrive rather than becoming an ignored backlog.
Retained information binding an operation identity to its accepted meaning and effect. Its retention and atomic relationship to the effect determine the scope of duplicate safety.
A deliberate reduction in supported capability, such as rejecting new mutations while serving status. It should remain explicit and observable rather than being disguised as ordinary success.
One transport or execution try for a logical operation. Several attempts can correspond to one retained business effect when the idempotency contract is preserved.
A controlled representation whose inputs, event order, and time can be reproduced. It supports reasoning about selected histories but does not automatically model all real-world failures.
An ordering token for membership information within a defined authority domain. Restarting or replacing that authority requires an explicit generation or continuity policy.
A lifecycle phase that stops new admission while settling already admitted work under a bounded policy. Resource destruction should follow completion or cancellation ownership, not precede it.
Persisted state representing an accepted obligation that can be resumed after process loss. In this book, pending gateway rows serve this role and drive later delivery.
The resource or protocol within which a business change is considered committed. A local database transaction cannot automatically include an email provider or another independent service.
A generation identifying an authority or state-machine interval. It lets a component reject stale completions or stale ownership, provided generation issuance and comparison are defined correctly.
The allowed amount of bad service outcomes under a specified objective, denominator, and window. It is a policy tool, not a substitute for correctness invariants.
A stable identifier for a domain occurrence. It should remain associated with the same meaning across redelivery and may need to survive changes in transport position.
A convergence-oriented contract under stated conditions. The label alone does not define intermediate reads, conflict resolution, uniqueness, or the treatment of externally visible promises.
An abstraction controlling where and when work runs. A coroutine does not automatically provide an executor, and serialized execution does not necessarily imply one fixed operating-system thread.
An ordered ownership generation checked by the protected resource to reject stale writers. It requires a trustworthy issuer and preserved state; a client-chosen integer is not authority.
The protocol mechanism that identifies message boundaries in a byte stream. TCP’s stream behavior does not preserve the boundaries of individual application writes.
A comparison ensuring that an asynchronous result still belongs to the state that may accept it. The result can remain informationally useful even when its state-update authority is stale.
A controlled transition that stops admission, settles or cancels work under policy, joins execution, and releases resources. It still needs a bounded fallback for uncooperative work.

A contract under which repeated attempts at the same defined operation do not create additional unintended effects. Identity scope, payload association, retention, and atomicity determine its actual guarantee.
Consumer-side retained state used to recognize already handled messages or operations. For crash-safe effect deduplication, its receipt must be atomic with the relevant local effect.
A property that must remain true across every supported state transition, including failure and recovery. Examples include stable key meaning and rejection of stale ownership generations.
Random variation applied to timing, often retry delays, to reduce synchronization among callers. It does not replace a rate, concurrency, or total resource budget.
Time-bounded authority under a coordinator’s rules. Lease expiration can permit reassignment but does not forcibly stop an old process or revoke every delayed external write.
A consistency contract in which each operation appears to take effect between invocation and completion while respecting real-time precedence. It is more specific than generic data validity.
An ordering mechanism based on events and communication rather than elapsed physical time. Increasing logical values do not by themselves prove causality between unrelated events.
The set of participants considered eligible under a service or coordination protocol. A local list is not automatically an authoritative or current view of the cluster.
A session property preventing observations from moving backward through already observed versions under the service’s defined conditions. Routing affinity alone may not preserve it after failure.
Producer-side durable state tying business intent to an outgoing delivery obligation. A dispatcher can replay it after failure, while the receiver still needs appropriate duplicate handling.
A condition in which some components or communication paths fail while others continue. It creates uncertainty that cannot be modeled as one process returning a single error code.
The value used to choose a data or work authority. It should align with the invariants and ordering scope that must remain local or coordinated.
Work that repeatedly fails for a persistent reason rather than a transient outage. It requires explicit terminal handling or repair to avoid indefinite retries and starvation.
A representation of verified identity and relevant claims used for authorization. Untrusted payload fields must not become a principal merely because they use familiar names.
Evidence describing how an artifact was produced, including relevant inputs and build process. A checksum establishes byte identity only relative to a trusted expected value.
A set of participants whose agreement satisfies a protocol’s rule. Intersection arithmetic is necessary for some designs but does not replace voting, persistence, log, or membership-transition rules.
Eligibility to receive a defined class of work. It differs from liveness and may change during dependency degradation, initialization, draining, or capacity exhaustion.

A controlled comparison and repair process among authoritative states after uncertainty or divergence. It should preserve evidence and authorization rather than silently overwrite conflicting meaning.
An authorized attempt to resume previously failed or quarantined work. It should preserve the original logical identity when recovering the same effect and record the reason and actor.
A selection method that scores key-candidate pairs and chooses a deterministic winner. Stable mapping properties do not copy state or authorize a new owner during migration.
Reprocessing retained work or events from a defined point. Pure projection rebuilds and external side effects require different policies so recovery does not accidentally repeat business actions.
A bound on attempts, elapsed time, rate, or another resource for recovery work. Multiple nested retry owners can multiply load beyond each layer’s apparent local limit.
A workflow that represents partial progress and coordinates recovery or compensation across independent effects. It is not a universal atomic transaction or automatic reversal of the world.
The ability of specified readers and writers to interpret stored or transmitted data with preserved meaning. Successful parsing is necessary but not sufficient when units or semantics change.
A measured definition of service behavior with a specified numerator, denominator, and boundary. Submission acceptance and accepted-job completion are different indicators in this volume.
A representation of state at a defined point. Recovery may require a matching log position, schema, receipt history, and authority generation; copying visible rows alone can be incomplete.
In asynchronous execution terminology, a mechanism for serializing associated handlers. It does not automatically imply a dedicated thread or solve object lifetime outside its execution contract.
Behavior in the slow portion of a latency distribution. A good average can coexist with unacceptable long waits, especially under queueing, contention, or periodic recovery work.
A rate-admission model with bounded burst capacity and replenishment. It controls a different resource dimension from simultaneous concurrency and queued memory.
Metadata used to connect spans across boundaries under a tracing standard. It is not a credential and should not grant authorization merely because a caller supplies it.
A result in which the caller cannot determine whether a remote effect committed. Stable identity, status lookup, and reconciliation can manage it without inventing a new operation.

A storage mechanism recording changes before they are incorporated into other serving structures. Its durability, checkpoint, backup, and recovery semantics depend on the implementation and configuration.

provenance: Imported from the supplied corrected EPUB and PDF pair. The reading preserves the EPUB spine, sections, examples, tables, and source wording. Extracted listings retain their source text; validation status distinguishes complete compiled programs from excerpts and platform-dependent material. The ZIP contains ebooks, not the separate original companion directories named by some book commands. The added study diagrams are identified as teaching views.
